summary:
# NOTES: *Thomas Wingfold, Curate*, Vol. II (George MacDonald; chs. I–XXXIV; ends "END OF THE SECOND VOLUME")

## Cast
- **Thomas Wingfold**: curate at the Abbey, Glaston; ~30; lodges near churchyard; honest doubter seeking God; sermons unscripted.
- **Rachel Polwarth**: hunchbacked niece, white garret room, cheerful, sick; "dwarfie"; temper she repents quickly; sees dreams of freedom.
- **Mr. Polwarth (uncle)**: hunchbacked gate-keeper at Osterfield Park lodge; poet; asthma; "pigeon-breast"; brother of Rachel's late father (mad, left manuscript).
- **Helen Lingard**: beautiful, tall, rides; nurses brother; secret: killed a woman; cousin of George; hides in dressing-room.
- **Leopold Lingard**: brother, ~20, dark, tropical (mother a dark-skinned woman, opium habit); "Poldie"; killed **Emmeline** (jilted Helen's brother); "the knife"; wants to confess.
- **George Bascombe**: barrister, Helen's cousin; materialist, hearty, "great rubbish"; courts Helen; "Hercules Bascombe" in narrator's aside.
- **Mrs. Ramshorn**: Helen/George's aunt, widow of late dean; clerical, disapproving.
- **Mr. Drew**: chief linen-draper, Pine Street; deacon at Drake's chapel; wife ran off ~20 years ago with traveller from Manchester house; sells print at cost to soldiers' wives.
- **Mr. Faber**: doctor.
- **Mr. Hooker**: county magistrate.
- Others: Miss Lingard's horse; Dives/Lazarus; Glaston Abbey; Pine Street; Osterfield Park; "the old house of Glaston" (uninhabited 20 years).

## Ch I – Rachel and her Uncle
- Dusk; Rachel opened gate for Miss Lingard and rider; no thanks.
- Rachel envies Miss Lingard's strength. Uncle: "content" vs "satisfied"; prayer is better than grumbling.
- Polwarth: individuality "like the onliness of God"; prays "Lord, it is thine."
- Rachel: "I don't mind being God's dwarf"; wants to be made over.
- Polwarth offers to read verses; Rachel says wait for Mr. Wingfold (Saturdays). Polwarth: "pearls before swine" → Rachel's temper; repents, kisses his hand. Uncle: "rough dirty shell."
- Rachel goes down to receive Wingfold.

## Ch II – A Dream
- Polwarth reads his poem (opening "Lord, hear my discontent"; "Thou only thinkest—I am thought"; ends "I in thy allness have my perfect share").
- Narrator aside: George Bascombe's "facts of life"; "AND HE CAN PROVE IT."
- Wingfold: can't follow verse; asks copy; asks about Bible inspiration. Polwarth: "Is the man Christ Jesus we have to know."
- Polwarth's dream: Tauchnitz NT; Sinaitic MS (Tischendorf, Mount Sinai); word omitted. Dream: desert, Armenian convent, search for original fourth-gospel MS. Torn curtain, stone cell, closed book. The apostle John (blue-veined hand) burns the book on altar fire. Words: "the Word of God liveth... in the heart of the man that in love obeyeth him." Polwarth awoke weeping.
- Wingfold: "I trust I have the lesson too." Leaves.

## Ch III – Another Sermon
- Narrator: Wingfold's awakening; Conscience on the guard's seat, Will on reins, Imagination the outrider with dog Fancy.
- Crowds come to church.
- Sermon 2: "I dare not call myself a Christian." Subscribed Articles unthinkingly. Texts: love enemies; be perfect; lay not up treasures; take no thought; judge not; do unto others; "Not every one that saith Lord, Lord."

## Ch IV – Nursing
- Mrs. Ramshorn: sermon makes him "prove himself a pagan."
- Bascombe: "I like the fellow... great rubbish." Suggests inviting Wingfold; aunt refuses ("abusing us"); Helen smiles.
- Leopold's dejection; Faber suspects softening of brain; Helen suggests withdrawal of narcotic.
- Helen sits up nights, 1–3 a.m. worst; moves bed to dressing-room.
- Reading: Grimm tale (murder) rejected; Thousand and One Nights.
- Bascombe visits Saturdays–Mondays.
- Leopold's sleep-talk: "Oh Helen, darling, give me my knife. Why will you not let me die?"

## Ch V – Glaston and the Curate
- Town gossip: fanatic, Romanizer, vanity, "softening of the brain."
- Wingfold's doubt; his "aurora"; Polwarth: "too good to be true?"
- Wingfold's poem (O Lord, if on the wind...; signs/wonders).
- Bascombe pronounces him a hypochondriac.

## Ch VI – The Linen-Draper
- Drew invites Wingfold upstairs (smells of tobacco). Wingfold blunders re "Mrs. Drew"; she left him ~20 years ago with another.
- Drew uneasy about profits; "How would Jesus have done as a draper?" Sees sermon; had tried "do as you would be done by."
- Wingfold: "Jesus buying and selling"; trade as sacred.
- Wingfold: "Did you think to try praying, Mr. Drew?"

## Ch VII – Rachel
- Wingfold asks Polwarth to bring Drew to tea.
- Rachel's white room; "poor dwarfie"; sheep on altar image; "IF there be a God."
- Rachel's dreams: freedom, haemony flower (Comus), angel instrument; "crooked as a crab, nearly as lame as a seal."
- Polwarth: "crooked rose-tree"; father's "overblown" rose; father's strange manuscript.
- "Ye are the temples of the Holy Ghost." Rachel: "Some of us a little ruinous!"

## Ch VIII – The Butterfly
- Wingfold walking home reflects on God and suffering; nature; sonnet "Methought I floated sightless..." Then a demon of commonplace.

## Ch IX – The Common-Place
- Drew's shop at evening; sells print at cost to soldiers' wives (10 years, secret).
- Drew's history: wife daughter of doctor, married for bread; she "despised my trade"; "demon of selfishness sevenfold."
- Shop feels like chapel; hymn "Let me stand ever at the door."
- Wingfold: "God forbid!" (re Drew's "ludicrous" thought of God in shop).
- Drew keeps pew and subscription, gives up deaconship. Wingfold: don't proselytize.

## Ch X – Home Again
- Wingfold meets Bascombe; "if what I find should be true, even though you should never be able to see it."
- Sonnet "Methought that in a solemn church I stood" (woman sweeping; "Daughter, thou sweepest well my floor").
- Churchyard stone.

## Ch XI – The Sheath
- Polwarth's confidence (asks secrecy even from Rachel).
- Night walk; cry; old house of Glaston; tall woman rushed past; third cry; closet door; lady's voice soothing a youth's; youth's despair.
- Next morning: room empty; a small leather **knife-sheath** found behind bedstead. Polwarth gives it to Wingfold.
- Wingfold thinks of Helen's pale face.

## Ch XII – Invitation
- Wingfold on human suffering; "COME UNTO ME ALL YE THAT LABOUR..." (Matt 11:28).

## Ch XIII – A Sermon to Helen
- Sunday: Wingfold sees Helen, Bascombe, Mrs. Ramshorn, Drew, Polwarth, Rachel.
- Sermon: Jesus and the weary; "I dare not say I know there is a Father... this man says HE KNOWS"; yoke = learn his obedience.

## Ch XIV – A Sermon to Himself
- Helen sobs; Bascombe annoyed; Polwarth and Rachel weep.
- Wingfold's poem "Yes, Master, when thou comest thou shalt find / A little faith on earth".

## Ch XV – Criticism
- Mrs. Ramshorn: "infidel or fanatic? Jesuit or Socinian?"
- Bascombe: needs composition; "Methodists would treasure him."
- Garden: Bascombe rebukes Helen; "Jew-gospel"; "idiot"; "Havannah"; "anni domini 1870."
- Helen: "the old fable pretends... to provide help for sore hearts."
- Bascombe: "to live for others." Helen: "no God to look after the business."

## Ch XVI – A Vanishing Glimmer
- Helen tells Leopold of sermon. Leopold: "She is DEAD—I killed her."; "Then he ain't fit to be God!"; "You had better tell that to the jury."
- Helen briefly despises him; only hope is Bascombe's death doctrine.

## Ch XVII – Let Us Pray!
- Helen resolves to consult Wingfold, disguised as hypothetical.
- Leopold (Satan / crown-jewels joke). Helen's Sandwich Islands fantasy.
- Helen: "you can pray... let us die together."
- Helen sings "Comfort ye," "Come unto me" at piano, "Thou didst not leave" ("Maenad"). Kneels by brother.

## Ch XVIII – Two Letters
- Helen's letter (asks meeting; P.S. Pine Street 11 o'clock tomorrow). Wingfold meets her briefly; hands pamphlet with letter.
- Wingfold's reply: meet at Polwarth cottage. Garden honeysuckle seat.

## Ch XIX – Advice in the Dark
- Helen veiled: "haunting idea." Wingfold: "Do you call yourself a Christian?" "No."
- "Suppose it were a great wrong." Reparation impossible? Confession? "Are you sure... he is not neglecting something he ought to do?"
- Helen goes white. Wingfold: "at least confession—"

## Ch XX – Intercession
- Helen faints. Polwarth kneels and prays: "Life eternal... thou art in her heart."
- Helen flees home through trees; Wingfold follows.
- Polwarth: people seek advice hoping adviser agrees with "second familiar self."

## Ch XXI – Helen Alone
- Summer-house. Helen's thoughts on guilt, publicity, God; "Her Poldie on the scaffold!"
- Prays; housekeeper: Leopold restless.

## Ch XXII – A Haunted Soul
- Leopold: wants Mr. Wingfold; "I saw her!"; Emmeline's back in wardrobe mirror, worm on shoulder.
- Helen: "Let her come then!" Leopold: "if you don't let me see Mr. Wingfold, I shall go mad, and then everything will come out."

## Ch XXIII – Compelled Confidence
- Helen goes to park; finds Wingfold; "Are you quite honest with me?"
- Wingfold shows the **sheath**; Helen snatches it. "You have been acting the spy."
- Helen kneels: "promise me you will not make him give himself up." Wingfold won't promise.
- Helen: "He is NOT wicked—my poor darling... only twenty."
- Wingfold: "May God be to me as I am to him!"

## Ch XXIV – Willing Confidence
- Wingfold sees Leopold; embraces him. "I knew you would come." "I saw you come in close behind HER."
- Leopold's full confession (narrative in direct speech): killed Emmeline; wants to be hanged; "if I had killed myself instead."
- Leopold: "I fancy she loves George Bascombe... who would marry the sister of a murderer?"

## Ch XXV – The Curate's Counsel
- Wingfold: "Shame is not defilement"; "Let us keep our shame and be made clean."
- Leopold: "Emmeline is not in the dark grave." Wingfold: "if there be a God, she is in his hands."
- Wingfold: see Jesus; "I AM WITH YOU ALWAYS"; "COME UNTO ME"; "if he will not do it... wrongly named Jesus."
- Wingfold leaves; Leopold hides face.

## Ch XXVI – Sleep
- Helen on stair; Wingfold weeps. "He is the wisest and best man I have ever known" (of Polwarth).
- Helen: must ask Leopold about Polwarth. Leopold had fallen asleep; "Did God make me sleep, Helen?"
- Leopold: "that IS a good fellow." Helen's jealousy. Leopold recalls first meeting Helen as a boy-foreigner.

## Ch XXVII – Divine Service
- Mrs. Ramshorn blocks window during Wingfold's visit; Leopold arranges next-day talk.
- Wingfold brings Drew to Polwarth; Rachel: "We'll see what God will do for me."
- Polwarth on "divine service": child at father's knee; prayer is communion, not service; shop = temple; counter = altar; "holy moderation"; "your calling is to do the best for your neighbour."
- Drew: "I must live; I cannot give my goods away."

## Ch XXVIII – A Shop in Heaven
- Rachel reads Polwarth's dictated vision (narrator "guide," Vision of Mirza style): city of righteous; streams; shop of silks; buyers take goods unpaid; no coin or books; a shopkeeper kneels in prayer over greed; guide: "No man here doeth service for advantage"; those who fail to repent get reincarnated as lower life.
- Wingfold: "I think that COULD be!" Drew: "Not in this world." Polwarth: doubting it is doubting the kingdom.

## Ch XXIX – Polwarth and Lingard
- Leopold dresses; asks for Wingfold. Wingfold brings Polwarth (cowslip "rubies" from Midsummer Night's Dream).
- Polwarth to Leopold: forgiveness; "watchmaker" simile; God can set right what he made wrong.
- Leopold: "I wish to give myself up." Asks Wingfold for magistrate.
- Helen: "Leave the house!" Falls on knees: "If you do not save Leopold, I will kill myself." Curse; "Amen!"
- Leopold: "God has heard me!"; another man may be accused; then collapses. Men leave by window; Helen says "Go, I beg of you."

## Ch XXX – The Strong Man
- Saturday: George Bascombe visits. "You'll be as blind as the fish in the cave of Kentucky."
- George: Leopold is "quite off his head"; plans Monday visit to Mr. Hooker; wants Wingfold excluded; suspects curate's influence.
- Helen lies down, exhausted.

## Ch XXXI – George and Leopold
- Leopold dreams "Emmeline!"; asks about hanging ("choking"); George's Stoic answer: "What's done is done."
- Leopold trusts George (thinks him Helen's suitor).
- George reflects on Helen's danger; "Helen had the vampyre of an imperfect love."
- Wingfold called; turned away by butler; left "like a vulture."

## Ch XXXII – Wingfold and Helen
- Helen's thoughts: George's influence; Leopold should die believing Wingfold's way.
- Library: Wingfold: "I am far more afraid of your influence than of his." Helen: "I would die for him."
- Wingfold: "Then at least let your pride die for him." Helen leaves; later admits he is right.

## Ch XXXIII – A Review
- Wingfold's "curate's chair" (stone by yew, churchyard). Narrator reflects on his spiritual change (golden weathercock "Peter-cock"; Christ as living presence).
- Poem "Father, I cry to thee for bread."

## Ch XXXIV – A Sermon to Leopold (end of Vol. II)
- Sunday sermon "I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance."
- Peter: "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man."
- Narrator's dream of crime: guilt, then awakening; repentance makes "a new creature"; "the murderer and the unloving sit on the same bench."
- Closing call: "Come and repent... he came not to call the righteous, but sinners, us, you and me."
